dct_description_sm: The influence of abiotic factors such as temperature and precipitations on the phenology of plants (i.e.: flowering, growth and senescence) in temperate forest and grassland ecosystems has been well described in the last decades at species and continental scales. However, a lack of information still persists regarding the factors regulating plant phenology in wetlands and at plant community level in general. Therefore, the aim of this study is to identify the biotic (i.e. species identity and diversity) and abiotic factors (temperature, soil moisture, soil texture properties and soil pH) regulating the phenology of wetland plant communities. Our hypothesis is that a combination of biotic and abiotic factors should be important drivers of wetland plant communities' phenology. However biotic factors such as plant species identity and plant species richness should have a stronger influence on the dynamic of the phenology of plant communities than abiotic factors.
dct_title_s: Phenology of wetland plant communities, Umiujaq, Nunavik
